ideas: How you studied English at school
What changed when you started learning independently
Your current habits and remaining challenges
model: I started learning English in grade three, like most children in Vietnam, but for a long time I didn't really learn to use it. At school, lessons used to focus almost entirely on grammar drills and reading short texts. We would memorise lists of words and fill in endless multiple-choice exercises, so it was mostly rote learning. As a result, I could get good marks in exams, but whenever I met a foreigner, I'd get completely tongue-tied. The turning point came in my second year of university, when I joined an English club. For the first time, I had to actually speak, and I realised how little I could say. After that, I changed my approach. I started to immerse myself in English as much as possible. I'd watch American sitcoms with English subtitles, listen to podcasts on the bus and chat with people in online forums. I picked up a lot of vocabulary that way, especially everyday expressions that textbooks never taught. These days I no longer study grammar from books very much. Instead, I use English at work every day, and I practise speaking with apps like this one. I'd say I've made steady progress, but I still have a long way to go, especially with pronunciation and speaking fluently under pressure. My goal now is to reach band seven in IELTS, so I'm trying to practise a little bit every single day.
